items.title: the PLAYGROUND's examples are broken on v0.42.0: they still spell the reactive `.map` that A142 renamed to `.derive` (and whatever else the pipe model changed)
items.discussion: the owner (2026-10-01); A142 S1 (`map` → `derive`, move-only pipes), I9 (`HashMap`/`HashSet`), Order 44's seal (the playground SMOKE program had the same `.map` and reddened CI's wasm leg; fixed at 170562b9 — the examples themselves were not swept), `sweeps/order44/reactive-44/playground-reactive-44.patch`
items.body: Sweep every example the playground ships (and any snippet it loads from the site) against the released compiler: `.map` on a source → `.derive`, a derived value consumed once (`.memo()`/`.cell()` where it is read twice), `Map`/`Set` → `HashMap`/`HashSet`, tracked reads where the old examples nested `.get()`. Check whether reactive-44's playground patch was ever applied. GATE so it cannot recur: a test (playground repo CI, or vilan's wasm smoke) that compiles EVERY shipped example with the wasm compiler and fails on any diagnostic. Sizing S.

the vilan SITE, the PLAYGROUND and the DOCS use ELEMENT SYNTAX (`
…
`) wherever it applies, instead of `view("div")` builder chains
items.discussion: the owner (2026-10-01); A46 (fragments) and the element-syntax arc; kolt and `lucide/lib.vl` already write it; K25 (the playground examples' sweep — do both in one pass over the playground)
items.body: Scope: vilan-website's own source, every playground example, the book/std docs' UI snippets and the examples directory's UI programs. Where it applies: a statically-shaped element tree. Where it does not (say so in a short style note in the docs): a dynamically chosen tag, a builder passed around as a value, a chain that is mostly reactive bindings — decide the rule from what reads better, write it down once, apply it uniformly. No behaviour change: emitted output stays identical where the desugar is the same (the site's build and the doc snippets' tests are the proof). `vilan fmt` formats the result. Sizing M; a docs/web lane.
